title: Hebrews Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Hebrews 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Melchisedec is mentioned first in Hebrews 7:1 as the king of Salem and priest of the most high God.

questions.question: Who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings?
questions.explanation: Melchisedec is the one who met Abraham as stated in Hebrews 7:1.

questions.question: What did Abraham give to Melchisedec?
questions.explanation: Abraham gave a tenth part of all to Melchisedec as stated in Hebrews 7:2.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 7:2, what is Melchisedec also called?
questions.explanation: Melchisedec is interpreted as King of righteousness in Hebrews 7:2.

questions.question: What is stated about Melchisedec's parentage?
options: He is without father and mother
He is a descendant of Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: He is without father and mother
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:3 states that Melchisedec is without father, without mother, without descent.

questions.question: Who gave tithes according to the law?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:5 mentions that the sons of Levi have a commandment to take tithes.

questions.question: Who received tithes from Abraham?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:6 indicates that Melchisedec received tithes from Abraham.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 7:7 state about the blessing?
options: The better is blessed by the less
The less is blessed by the better
questions.correctAnswer: The less is blessed by the better
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:7 states that without all contradiction, the less is blessed of the better.

questions.question: In Hebrews 7:8, what is said about men who receive tithes?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:8 states that here men that die receive tithes.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 7:9, who paid tithes in Abraham?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:9 mentions that Levi also paid tithes in Abraham.

questions.question: In what state was Levi when Melchisedec met Abraham?
options: He was yet in the loins of his father
questions.correctAnswer: He was yet in the loins of his father
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:10 states that Levi was yet in the loins of his father when Melchisedec met Abraham.

questions.question: True or False: Melchisedec is described as having no beginning of days.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:3 states that Melchisedec has neither beginning of days nor end of life.

questions.question: True or False: Abraham received tithes from Melchisedec.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:6 indicates that Melchisedec blessed Abraham and received tithes from him.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that Melchisedec was a descendant of Levi.
questions.explanation: The text does not state that Melchisedec was a descendant of Levi; rather, it states he whose descent is not counted from them.

questions.question: True or False: Melchisedec was the king of Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: The text refers to Melchisedec as the king of Salem, not Jerusalem.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What further need was there for another priest to arise after the order of Melchisedec?
options: Because the Levitical priesthood was perfect
Because perfection was not by the Levitical priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: Because perfection was not by the Levitical priesthood
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 7:11 states that if perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, there would be no need for another priest after Melchisedec.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 7:12 promise will happen if the priesthood is changed?
options: There is a change of the law
There is no change in the law
questions.correctAnswer: There is a change of the law
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:12 clearly states that with the change of the priesthood, there is a necessity for a change of the law.

questions.question: Which tribe is mentioned as the one from which no man attended at the altar?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:13 specifies that the one being spoken of pertains to another tribe, which is Judah, as no one from Judah served at the altar.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 7:14 indicate about Jesus' lineage?
options: He was from the tribe of Levi
He was from the tribe of Judah
He was a descendant of Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: He was from the tribe of Judah
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:14 confirms that it is evident our Lord sprang out of Judah, which was not associated with priesthood according to Moses.

questions.question: What is said to arise after the similitude of Melchisedec?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:15 states that after the similitude of Melchisedec, there arises another priest.

questions.question: How was the new priest made according to Hebrews 7:16?
options: After the law of a carnal commandment
After the power of an endless life
questions.correctAnswer: After the power of an endless life
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:16 indicates that the new priest was made not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 7:17 testify about the new priest?
options: He is a priest for a season
He is a priest like Aaron
He is a priest only for Judah
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:17 testifies that the new priest is a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 7:18 say about the commandment going before?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:18 states that there is a verily disannulling of the commandment going before because of its weakness and unprofitableness.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 7:19, what did the law made nothing perfect bring?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:19 indicates that the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope is what allows us to draw near to God.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 7:20 mention about the priesthood?
options: It was established without an oath
It was established with an oath
questions.correctAnswer: It was established with an oath
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:20 mentions that he was made priest not without an oath, indicating the significance of the oath in establishing the priesthood.

questions.question: What is the significance of the order of Melchisedec in relation to the faith of believers?
questions.explanation: The order of Melchisedec signifies an eternal priesthood, as shown by the references to Jesus being a priest forever.

questions.question: How does the change in priesthood reflect on the believer's relationship with God?
options: It allows for a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It allows for a new covenant
questions.explanation: The change in priesthood implies the establishment of a new covenant, offering believers a better hope and relationship with God.

questions.question: True or False: The law is described as making nothing perfect.
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Hebrews 7:19, which asserts that the law made nothing perfect.

questions.question: True or False: Melchisedec was a descendant of Levi.
questions.explanation: This is false because Hebrews 7:6 indicates that Melchisedec's descent is not counted from Levi.

questions.question: True or False: The priesthood of Jesus is likened to that of Aaron.
questions.explanation: This is false as Hebrews 7:11 contrasts the priesthood of Melchisedec with that of Aaron, highlighting the uniqueness of Jesus' priesthood.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 7.

questions.question: Who is described as having an unchangeable priesthood?
questions.explanation: This man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. (Hebrews 7:24)

questions.question: According to Hebrews 7, who is able to save to the uttermost?
questions.explanation: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him. (Hebrews 7:25)

questions.question: What did Jesus do once for all when he offered up himself?
questions.explanation: For this he did once, when he offered up himself. (Hebrews 7:27)

questions.question: What is the significance of the oath mentioned in Hebrews 7?
questions.explanation: But this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever. (Hebrews 7:21)

questions.question: What does Jesus represent according to Hebrews 7:22?
questions.explanation: By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament. (Hebrews 7:22)

questions.question: How does Hebrews 7 describe the high priest that was made by an oath?
questions.explanation: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens. (Hebrews 7:26)

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'hierus' in Hebrews 7:26 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'hierus' translates to 'priest,' signifying one who offers sacrifices.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Hebrews 7:17 when it states, 'Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec'?
questions.explanation: This statement reflects typology, where Melchisedec serves as a foreshadowing of Christ's eternal priesthood.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of Jesus as a high priest?
questions.explanation: Psalm 110:4 states, 'The Lord hath sworn and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec,' affirming Jesus’ priesthood.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage emphasizes the need for a new covenant?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31 prophesies a new covenant, which aligns with the better testament mentioned in Hebrews 7:22.

questions.question: What comes before Hebrews 7:25?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:25 follows after stating that Jesus has an unchangeable priesthood, as mentioned in Hebrews 7:24.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 7:18 say about the law?
questions.explanation: For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof. (Hebrews 7:18)

questions.question: The statement 'For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity' is found in which verse?
questions.explanation: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath makes the Son. (Hebrews 7:28)

questions.question: True or False: Jesus needs to offer daily sacrifices for his own sins.
questions.explanation: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins. (Hebrews 7:27)

questions.question: True or False: Melchisedec was a king and a priest.
questions.explanation: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God. (Hebrews 7:1)

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 7:3 teach about the eternal priesthood of Christ?
options: Christ's priesthood is eternal and uninterrupted, unlike the Levitical priests who are mortal.
Christ's priesthood is temporary and dependent on the Mosaic Law.
Christ's priesthood is limited to earthly ministry only and ends with His ascension.
Christ's priesthood is conditional upon human obedience.
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's priesthood is eternal and uninterrupted, unlike the Levitical priests who are mortal.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:3 says Christ is 'without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually,' emphasizing His eternal and unchanging priesthood.

questions.question: What doctrine about the insufficiency of the Levitical priesthood is taught in Hebrews 7:11?
options: The Levitical priesthood could not bring perfection, necessitating a new priest after the order of Melchisedec.
The Levitical priesthood was fully sufficient and needed no replacement.
The Levitical priesthood was superior and everlasting.
The Levitical priesthood was only symbolic and never functional.
questions.correctAnswer: The Levitical priesthood could not bring perfection, necessitating a new priest after the order of Melchisedec.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:11 states that if perfection were possible through the Levitical priesthood, there would be no need for another priest after the order of Melchisedec, indicating its insufficiency.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's priesthood and the law is taught in Hebrews 7:12?
options: A change in priesthood necessitates a change in the law.
The law remains unchanged regardless of priesthood.
The priesthood changes but the law remains the same.
The law is superior to the priesthood and never changes.
questions.correctAnswer: A change in priesthood necessitates a change in the law.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:12 teaches that when the priesthood changes, 'there is made of necessity a change also of the law,' linking priesthood and law inseparably.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 7:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:21 shows God's covenant faithfulness as He swears an oath that Christ is priest forever, 'The Lord sware and will not repent,' demonstrating His unchanging commitment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by Christ's eternal priesthood in Hebrews 7:24?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:24 states that Christ 'continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood,' pointing to God's attribute of immutability — unchanging nature.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 7:1 connect the Melchisedec priesthood to Abrahamic promises elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It reveals Melchisedec as a type of Christ who blesses Abraham, linking to the Abrahamic covenant.
It shows Melchisedec as a rival to Abraham's faith.
It denies any connection between Melchisedec and the Abrahamic promises.
It presents Melchisedec as a minor historical figure unrelated to Scripture's redemptive themes.
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals Melchisedec as a type of Christ who blesses Abraham, linking to the Abrahamic covenant.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:1 shows Melchisedec meeting and blessing Abraham, highlighting a priesthood connected to God's promises to Abraham, prefiguring Christ's priesthood.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 7:16 anticipate Christ's priesthood as superior to the Levitical order in redemptive history?
options: By emphasizing that Christ's priesthood is based on the power of an endless life, surpassing the temporary Levitical priesthood.
By affirming Christ is a Levitical priest by descent.
By denying Christ's priesthood and focusing on the Mosaic covenant.
By suggesting Christ's priesthood is less effective than the Levitical priests.
questions.correctAnswer: By emphasizing that Christ's priesthood is based on the power of an endless life, surpassing the temporary Levitical priesthood.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:16 contrasts Christ's priesthood, 'not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life,' showing its superiority and permanence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 7:18 and Hebrews 7:19 teach about the law and hope?
options: The old law is annulled for weakness, and a better hope through Christ brings true perfection.
The law is perfect and needs no replacement by hope.
Hope is irrelevant to the law's purpose of perfection.
The law and hope are identical and unchanging.
questions.correctAnswer: The old law is annulled for weakness, and a better hope through Christ brings true perfection.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:18-19 state the previous commandment is annulled due to weakness and that the law made nothing perfect, but a better hope brings us near to God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about priesthood and oath is presented in Hebrews 7:20 and Hebrews 7:21?
options: Christ's priesthood is confirmed by a divine oath, unlike priests made without an oath.
All priests have equal status regardless of oath.
The oath is irrelevant to the legitimacy of priesthood.
The Levitical priests received a stronger oath than Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's priesthood is confirmed by a divine oath, unlike priests made without an oath.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:20-21 distinguishes Christ's priesthood, established 'not without an oath' but by God's unchangeable promise, unlike the Levitical priests.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 7:23 and Hebrews 7:25 teach about Jesus' priesthood and salvation?
options: Unlike mortal priests who die, Jesus lives forever and can save completely those who come to God through Him.
Jesus' priesthood is temporary and limited in saving power.
Priests and Jesus have the same limitation in salvation.
Salvation does not depend on Jesus' eternal priesthood.
questions.correctAnswer: Unlike mortal priests who die, Jesus lives forever and can save completely those who come to God through Him.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:23-25 contrasts the many mortal priests with Jesus' eternal priesthood, highlighting His ability to save to the uttermost.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Hebrews 7:27 teaches Christ needed daily sacrifices like Levitical priests. What does the text actually teach?
options: Christ offered Himself once for all, not needing daily sacrifices.
Christ's sacrifice was repeated daily in heaven.
Christ's sacrifice was ineffective compared to Levitical sacrifices.
questions.correctAnswer: Christ offered Himself once for all, not needing daily sacrifices.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:27 clearly states Christ 'needeth not daily... to offer up sacrifice... for this he did once, when he offered up himself,' negating the skeptics' claim.

questions.question: What doctrine about the priestly qualifications of Christ is taught in Hebrews 7:26?
options: Christ is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
Christ shares the same sinful nature as other priests.
Christ is an ordinary human with no special priestly qualifications.
Christ's priesthood is based on human merit.
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:26 describes the high priest who 'became us' as possessing these divine qualities, emphasizing His unique priestly nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 7:25 demonstrate about Christ's ongoing intercession?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:25 states Christ 'ever liveth to make intercession for them,' demonstrating His eternal priestly ministry.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 7:13 show Christ's priesthood relates to the tribal distinctions of Israel?
options: Christ belongs to a different tribe (Judah), not the Levitical tribe, showing a new priestly order.
Christ is from the tribe of Levi and follows its priesthood.
Tribal distinctions are irrelevant to priesthood.
Christ is from a non-Israelite tribe.
questions.correctAnswer: Christ belongs to a different tribe (Judah), not the Levitical tribe, showing a new priestly order.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:13 states Christ 'pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar,' highlighting the uniqueness of His priesthood.

questions.question: What doctrinal significance does Hebrews 7:22 assign to Jesus as a surety?
options: Jesus is a mere symbol without covenant power.
Jesus' role as surety is limited to earthly matters.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:22 calls Jesus 'a surety of a better testament,' underscoring His role as mediator of a superior covenant.
